assessment: Confirmed that Reopened is persisted and treated as active by BusinessDayRules.IsActive and BusinessDayGate.TryGetActiveAsync; ReopenBusinessDayHandler sets Status=Reopened and resets the closing checklist; CloseBusinessDayHandler accepts Reopened→Closing and evaluates blockers. OwnerDashboardQueryService.LoadAttentionAsync separately selects only Status=Open for both age and blocker evaluation and emits HasOpenBusinessDay=false, OpenBusinessDayAgeDays=null, CloseBlockerCount=0 when no Open row is found. No source evidence establishes that Reopened should intentionally be excluded from close-attention indicators; the reopened checklist reset and allowed close transition support treating it as a day awaiting closure. However DTO naming/comments describe currently Open, and ControlCenter provides direct list/get/checklist/blocker-preview access for a specified reopened day, so the issue is limited to the owner-dashboard summary indicators rather than a global inability to inspect/close the day. Candidate is suitable only at low severity pending product intent; no financial-close blockage or lost data proven.
counterevidence: AttentionDto names HasOpenBusinessDay/OpenBusinessDayAgeDays and documents the age for the currently open day, which could encode a strict Open-only presentation contract.
ControlCenterQueryService lists/get business days regardless of state and exposes blocker preview/checklist by explicit day ID, providing a separate inspection path.

Existing OwnerDashboardVerticalSliceTests assert ordinary Open behavior; no inspected dashboard test covers Reopened. BusinessDayCloseVerticalSliceTests proves reopen and checklist reset but not dashboard projections.

recommendation: Keep as a bounded dashboard-summary divergence candidate. Clarify intended meaning of Open-only indicators; then either query the shared active-day status set for age/blockers or explicitly document/test that dashboard attention intentionally covers only Open status while Reopened day obligations appear only in Control Center.
